events.title: September NFP / Employment Situation (pre-release)
events.why_it_matters: First payrolls print after the Sept 16 hike to 3.75–4.00%; consensus is +90k (FactSet/Reuters) with U3 unchanged at 4.1% after ADP +90k, and it is the last major labor print before the Oct 27–28 FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Beat vs miss versus +90k, wage growth (~+0.3% m/m / ~3.1–3.2% y/y), and revisions; a hot print would reverse the slide in October hike odds from ~70% to ~25%.

events.title: US–Iran war: ceasefire talks still stalled after Trump rejected 7-day Hormuz plan
events.why_it_matters: Seven-month war plus a US naval blockade and disrupted Strait of Hormuz flows keep a regime-level oil/inflation premium in place; Trump has rejected Iran's 7-day reopen-Hormuz proposal and warned the war ends 'one way or another'.
events.what_to_watch: Mediator sequencing (blockade/sanctions relief vs Hormuz reopen), any US force movements or strike threats around midterms, and tanker/flow data through Hormuz.

events.title: Brent holds near $100–102 on Iran-war risk premium
events.why_it_matters: Brent around $101–102 is a consumer tax and the main input to sticky headline CPI/HICP, even as crude flows have partially recovered via bypass pipelines while refined products remain tighter.
events.what_to_watch: Intraday swings on talk headlines, diesel/gasoline cracks, and whether OPEC+ hold vs unwind interacts with war-disrupted actual output.

events.title: Eurozone September flash HICP (energy-led spike)
events.why_it_matters: National flashes (DE 3.3%, FR 3.4%, IT 4.1%, ES 5.0%) point to euro-area headline near 3.8% y/y vs 3.2% in August, the hottest since 2023 and a test of the ECB's 'measured' post-September-hike hold.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs core split; if core stays ~2.4–2.5% the ECB can still skip October 29, but a broad overshoot would pull December hike odds up.

events.title: OPEC+ ministerial: November output expected unchanged
events.why_it_matters: Sources expect the eight/seven core producers to hold November targets after finishing the 1.65 mb/d unwind; actual barrels remain well below quotas because of Iran-war disruptions, so the signal matters more than the math.
events.what_to_watch: Any surprise increase, language on the remaining ~2 mb/d cut layer, and the 2027 capacity/quota review.

events.title: ISM Services PMI (September)
events.why_it_matters: Services are the bulk of US activity; consensus clusters near 55.0 after August 55.4, so a sharp drop would validate labor-market slowing while prices-paid would feed the oil-inflation debate.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs employment and prices-paid sub-indexes versus ~55 consensus.

events.title: FOMC minutes of Sept 15–16 25 bp hike
events.why_it_matters: Minutes will show how close the Committee was to 50 bp vs 25 bp and the bar for another move; markets have already repriced October hike odds down to ~25% after Williams said there is 'no need for urgency'.
events.what_to_watch: Dissent, discussion of oil/energy shock vs labor cooling, and any language that re-opens a back-to-back October hike.

events.title: Graham Act: USTR notification due on Russia/Iran secondary tariffs
events.why_it_matters: The Sept 18 law mandates up to 500% tariffs on Russian goods and up to 100% secondary tariffs on top buyers of Russian energy / sanctions-evasion facilitators, with congressional notification due ~Oct 8 and imposition by ~Oct 18 — a live China/India trade shock.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Trump uses full statutory rates or waivers, and whether China/India are named among the top-five purchasers.

events.title: PepsiCo Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: First major staples print of Q3 season; tests whether $100 oil, tariffs, and weak volumes are breaking pricing power.
events.what_to_watch: Organic volume vs price/mix, guidance, and any commentary on input costs and the US consumer.

events.title: University of Michigan consumer sentiment (prelim, October)
events.why_it_matters: Household inflation expectations and buying conditions are the transmission channel from $100 oil into demand destruction and Fed reaction.
events.what_to_watch: 1-year inflation expectations and current-conditions vs expectations split.

events.title: Q3 bank earnings kickoff — JPM, WFC, C, GS (Oct 13) and BAC (Oct 14)
events.why_it_matters: Big-bank results open Q3 season and set the tone for NII under a hiking Fed, credit quality, and capital-markets activity.
events.what_to_watch: Net interest income, charge-offs/reserving, trading/IB fees, and any guidance that assumes another 2026 hike.

events.title: UnitedHealth Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: UNH is the managed-care and Dow bellwether; medical-cost trend and 2027 guidance move the whole healthcare complex.
events.what_to_watch: Medical-cost ratio, Medicare Advantage commentary, and full-year outlook.

events.title: September existing-home sales
events.why_it_matters: Housing is the rate-sensitive sector most exposed to the 2026 hiking cycle and still-elevated mortgage rates.
events.what_to_watch: Sales vs inventory and median price; a further freeze would pressure homebuilders and regional banks.

events.title: China September trade data (exports/imports)
events.why_it_matters: Exports have been China's growth engine; the print shows whether tariff-truce front-running is still inflating shipments before the Jan 10, 2027 expiry.
events.what_to_watch: Export y/y vs August's boom, US-bound vs ASEAN/Taiwan mix, and import weakness as a domestic-demand signal.

events.title: September CPI — energy-driven headline, cooler core expected
events.why_it_matters: The pivotal print before the Oct 27–28 FOMC; TD/Continuum sketch headline +0.5–0.6% m/m (~3.7% y/y) on gasoline, with core ~+0.2% m/m — a hot headline/cool core split that can still reprice December.
events.what_to_watch: Core vs supercore services, energy contribution, and whether markets treat a 3.7% headline as oil noise or a hike lock-in.

events.title: ASML Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: ASML is the lithography chokepoint for AI-chip capacity; bookings and China mix are a leading indicator for the whole semi-equipment complex after Micron's blowout.
events.what_to_watch: Net bookings, 2027 capacity commentary, and China revenue/export-control mix.

events.title: September retail sales
events.why_it_matters: Shows whether the consumer is holding up under higher rates and ~$100 oil after a weak confidence backdrop.
events.what_to_watch: Control-group sales (ex-autos/gas) versus headline gasoline distortion.

events.title: September PPI
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline inflation after ISM prices-paid jumped to 77.9; a hot PPI would confirm oil/tariff pass-through into CPI with a lag.
events.what_to_watch: Final-demand core and energy/goods vs services split, same morning as retail sales.

events.title: SEMICON West 2026 (San Francisco)
events.why_it_matters: Flagship equipment/supply-chain gathering as the industry talks a path past $1T revenue; capex and HBM/CoWoS commentary can move the AI-hardware complex into ASML week.
events.what_to_watch: Tool-order color, advanced-packaging bottlenecks, and any China-export-control talk.

events.title: China mini-stimulus: PSL cut, relending quotas, first-time mortgage subsidies
events.why_it_matters: PBOC cut 1-year PSL 25 bp to 1.5%, raised tech/SME relending quotas, and started a 1 ppt first-time-buyer mortgage subsidy on Oct 1 — enough to defend the 4.5–5% GDP target, not a broad revival.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-through in credit impulse, property transactions after the subsidy, and whether Q3 GDP (due Oct 19, just outside this window) holds.

events.title: US–China trade truce extended to Jan 10, 2027; $60bn reciprocal tariff-relief lists
events.why_it_matters: Trump–Xi summit cut near-term tariff-cliff risk with a two-month truce extension and ~$30bn each way of non-sensitive goods (US toys/appliances; China ag/coal/devices) — soybeans and semis were excluded.
events.what_to_watch: Domestic implementation of the lists versus still-live Section 301 'forced labor' global tariffs in CIT.

events.title: CIT hearing on Trump Section 301 'forced labor' global tariffs
events.why_it_matters: Judges grilled USTR's near-blanket 10–12.5% tariffs covering ~99% of imports after SCOTUS struck IEEPA tariffs in Feb 2026; a loss would unwind the replacement tariff regime.
events.what_to_watch: Written decision in coming weeks and any stay; appeal path is the Federal Circuit.

events.title: Fed speakers (Williams, Jefferson) wash out October hike odds
events.why_it_matters: NY Fed's Williams said there is 'no need for urgency' and one more adjustment 'may be appropriate late in 2026'; October hike odds fell from ~70% to ~25%, shifting the live risk to December and to NFP/CPI surprises.
events.what_to_watch: Whether today's NFP reverses that message before the Oct 7 minutes.

events.title: Micron FY Q4 2026 record print validates AI-memory supercycle
events.why_it_matters: Revenue $54.23B and Q1 guide $61.5B ±$1.5B, with HBM largely committed into 2027, reset the memory/AI hardware complex and spilled into Samsung/SK hynix.
events.what_to_watch: Whether ASML bookings and SEMICON West capex talk confirm the bottleneck is packaging/HBM not demand.

events.title: South Korea September chip exports hit record $60.3bn
events.why_it_matters: Semi exports +262.8% y/y to $60.3bn, with SK hynix–TSMC HBM5/CoWoS validation, confirm AI-memory tightness is global not just a Micron story.
events.what_to_watch: KOSPI follow-through, HBM pricing, and any Taiwan packaging-capacity constraints.

events.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI 54.5 with prices-paid 77.9
events.why_it_matters: Ninth month of expansion (54.5 vs 54.6) but prices-paid jumped 6.8 pts to 77.9 on steel/aluminum, tariffs, and petroleum — a stagflation-lite signal into CPI.
events.what_to_watch: Whether PPI/CPI goods confirm that price spike or it stays in survey land.

events.title: Boeing SPEEA white-collar strike averted
events.why_it_matters: SPEEA approved a four-year deal (10% raise effective Oct 2), removing a strike risk to 737 MAX 10 / 777X certification and deliveries.
events.what_to_watch: Nothing immediate; production-ramp execution is now the residual risk.

events.title: Judge Mehta dismisses Chegg/Penske antitrust suits over Google AI Overviews
events.why_it_matters: A federal judge held that AI-search traffic diversion is not an antitrust 'agreement,' reducing near-term legal overhang on Google's AI search product (Epic/Play remedies still live).
events.what_to_watch: Appeal, and separate N.D. Cal. Epic injunction implementation.

events.title: Federal judge strikes down FTC expanded HSR premerger-notification rule
events.why_it_matters: Killing the expanded Hart-Scott-Rodino filing rule eases deal-friction for sponsors and strategics after a year of heavier merger review.
events.what_to_watch: FTC appeal and whether agencies shift to case-by-case challenges instead.

events.title: BoJ Summary of Opinions: debate on faster hikes after Sept move to 1.25%
events.why_it_matters: After the 25 bp hike to 1.25% (31-year high), the Oct 1 opinions showed members debating accelerating if inflation overshoots; next MPM is Oct 29–30 (just outside this window).
events.what_to_watch: Yen/JGB reaction and any leak ahead of the late-October Outlook Report.

events.title: FY2027 CR signed; Oct 1 shutdown averted through Dec 11
events.why_it_matters: H.R. 6500 funds government through Dec 11, so there is no October shutdown risk; the live fiscal fight is lame-duck plus a 2027 debt-ceiling X-date, with GOP floating a pre-emptive hike.
events.what_to_watch: Nothing this window; Dec 11 funding cliff and post-midterm debt-limit talk.

events.title: China official PMIs return to expansion (Sept 50.1/50.2)
events.why_it_matters: Manufacturing PMI 50.1 and non-manufacturing 50.2 flipped back above 50 just as the mini-stimulus landed, reducing tail risk of a hard Q3 miss.
events.what_to_watch: Whether October credit and property data confirm the PMI bounce.

top_risks: US–Iran war re-escalation or failed Hormuz sequencing that pushes Brent sustainably above $100 and into second-round inflation
Hot NFP today or hot core CPI on Oct 14 reversing the drop in Fed hike odds and lifting real yields
Graham Act secondary tariffs (~Oct 8 notice / ~Oct 18 imposition) hitting China/India as top buyers of Russian energy
Adverse CIT ruling (or a stay fight) on Section 301 global 'forced labor' tariffs that reopens the entire US tariff architecture
Energy-led euro-area HICP spike forcing the ECB off its October hold path and tightening global financial conditions
top_opportunities: Any credible US–Iran ceasefire / Hormuz reopen that collapses the oil-risk premium
Soft or in-line NFP that cements a Fed pause into year-end (October hike already ~25%)
AI-memory/semi complex: Micron guide + Korea export record + ASML + SEMICON West capex color
Implementation of the $60bn US–China non-sensitive tariff-relief lists without a new tariff-court shock
China mini-stimulus plus PMI expansion if property transactions actually respond to the Oct 1 mortgage subsidy
summary: The tape is still dominated by the US–Iran war and Brent near $101, but the policy overlay has shifted in 24 hours: Fed speakers have crushed October hike odds from ~70% to ~25%, so today's NFP and Oct 14 CPI are now pause-or-reprice events rather than a hike lock-in. A US–China truce extension and $60bn tariff-relief lists cut the near-term tariff cliff, while the Graham Act's mid-October secondary-tariff clock and the CIT challenge to Section 301 global tariffs keep trade-policy risk two-sided. Q3 earnings open with PepsiCo then the banks/UNH/ASML, against an AI-memory boom that Micron and Korean exports have already validated.
